question.worked_solution:
First, we write $2\,\frac{1}{7}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{1}{7}=\frac{(2\times 7)+1}{7}=\frac{15}{7}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}\times \frac{15}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5}\times \frac{15}{7} & =\frac{4}{7}\times \frac{15}{5} \\  & =\frac{4}{7}\times \text{ }3 \\  & =\frac{12}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{12}{7}=1\,\text{R}5=1\,\frac{5}{7}
$$
